photo.name: photographic print; cabinet card
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); cabinet card
photo.reason: Studio cabinet card portrait of Little Raven, an identified Arapaho chief, wearing hoop earrings and period dress; a documentary photograph of an Arapaho individual fits the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio profile portrait of Little Raven, a documented Arapaho chief, wearing traditional dress mixed with period clothing (hoop earrings, cloth shirt/vest/jacket); a documentary photo of an identified Arapaho individual clearly fits the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of "Bird Chief," identified as a war chief of the Arapahoes, wearing traditional dress including wrapped hair, ear ornaments, a blanket, and embroidered moccasins — this is a documentary photograph of Arapaho dress and identity, fitting the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: A documentary photograph of four Arapaho men, including Chief Friday, in traditional dress (buffalo robes, cloth shirts, moccasins) seated before a wagon at Leavenworth — a clear ethnographic record of Arapaho dress and life.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Yellow Calf, a named Arapaho chief, wearing an eagle-feather headdress, beaded tunic, and necklace — a clear documentary photo of Arapaho dress.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of "Bird Chief," identified as an Arapaho chief, wearing braided hair wrapped in cloth, hoop earrings, necklace, cloth shirt/vest, and a wool blanket — documentary photo of Arapaho dress and appearance.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Left Hand (Niwot), identified as an Arapaho chief, in traditional dress with braided hair, wool blanket, and tomahawk — a documentary photo of an Arapaho individual.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Heap of Bears, an Arapaho man, in traditional dress (braided hair, cloth shirt/vest, blanket) holding a tomahawk and decorated bag, taken by Alex Gardner in Washington, D.C. — a documentary photo of Arapaho dress and regalia, fitting the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Bird Chief, identified as an Arapaho chief, wearing braided hair, hoop earrings, cloth shirt/vest and a wrapped blanket—documentary photo of dress consistent with the claimed people.

painting-mss.name: Drawing
painting-mss.title: Night Skirmish (Henderson Ledger Artist A)
painting-mss.reason: A classic Plains ledger drawing of a mounted warrior in a skirmish, rendered in pencil and colored pencil on lined ledger paper, consistent with Arapaho ledger art of the 1880s.

painting-mss.name: Drawing
painting-mss.title: Two Riders Leading Horses (Henderson Ledger Artist B)
painting-mss.reason: This is a classic Plains ledger drawing showing two mounted warriors in regalia leading horses, drawn in pencil and colored pencil on lined ledger paper—consistent with Arapaho ledger art tradition, which continued into the reservation era with materials like this.

painting-mss.name: Drawing
painting-mss.title: Man and Two Women (Henderson Ledger Artist B)
painting-mss.reason: A classic Plains ledger drawing showing a man on horseback with regalia and two women in striped dress/blanket, consistent with Arapaho ledger art tradition of this period.

painting-mss.name: Drawing
painting-mss.title: Off to War (Henderson Ledger Artist B)
painting-mss.reason: Classic Plains ledger drawing of two warriors on horseback in feathered war bonnets/trailers with weapons, a well-known Arapaho ledger-art genre depicting war exploits; this matches the claimed Arapaho attribution and category.

painting-mss.name: Drawing
painting-mss.title: Self-Portrait
painting-mss.reason: The drawing shows a mounted warrior with feathered lance, shield, and regalia rendered on ledger paper — a classic Plains ledger-art self-portrait, consistent with Southern Arapaho authorship as recorded by the museum.

household.name: sadelväska
household.title: sadelväska
household.reason: A fringed hide saddlebag/quiver-like bag with classic Plains-style geometric beadwork (lazy-stitch box-and-border designs); the museum's own expert note attributes it to the Arapaho Plains homeland rather than the original Arizona/Hopi guess, matching the claimed ethnicity.

household.name: Skinnskrapa, skrapa
household.title: Skinnskrapa, skrapa
household.reason: A hide/skin scraper with an elk-antler handle, collected from the Cheyenne and Arapaho Reservation in Oklahoma — a typical Plains tool used and made by the Arapaho for processing hides.
